newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher, led by constructions.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher, led by constructions.

text.p: Taiwan share prices extended early gains to close higher on Wednesday, thanks to speculative late buying of construction and financial shares, brokers said.
The index ended up 40.95 points or 0.60 percent at its intraday high of 6,896.52. Turnover was slim at T$43.9 billion.
Constructions led the gains, rising 2.65 percent, with Prince Housing up T$1.3 to T$26.6.
Brokers said the late buying was largely speculative.
"Major investors likely tried to buy the heavily weighted financials and constructions to boost sentiment," said Alex Chen, assistant research manager at Wardley James Capel.
Brokers said the index was buoyed partly by reports that Morgan Stanley strategist Barton Biggs had recommended boosting holdings in Japan, non-Japan Asia and emerging markets.

"This gave investors some imagination room, with investors expecting foreign funds to enter to fuel the market," Chen said. "But it's impossible for foreign funds to immediately increase investment in the domestic stock market."
Textiles, especially polyester fabric makers, rose on expected rising orders likely transferred from South Korea, with Li Peng up by the daily seven percent limit to T$25.3.
Cement and plastic shares also rose, but electronics fell.
Computer monitor maker Mag Technology was limit-up to T$29.9 on its listing debut.
Brokers said they expected the index again would soon test the strong resistance at 7,000.
"Wednesday's move by major investors indicated their intention to push up the index to test 7,000 again," Chen said.
But breaking 7,000 will not be easy as fundamental economic improvements needed to hold share prices higher have not yet become fully apparent, he said.
For Thursday, the index was seen testing higher at 6,950.
